Stud Calculator

Wall length, stud spacing, openings and corners to the number of studs with waste, plus the plate length and how many boards to buy for the plates.

Your estimate

See products

Results update as you type. Studs are rounded up to whole pieces.

  • Counts every stud position, including both wall ends
  • Extra studs per opening and corner are editable assumptions
  • Runs in your browser

How to use the stud calculator

  1. Enter the wall length and height, and choose the stud spacing on center.
  2. Enter the number of door and window openings and corners. The extra studs for each are assumptions you can change to match your framing plan (for example, 2 king + 2 jack studs = 4 per opening).
  3. Set the number of plates and the board length you will buy for them, and a waste allowance for the studs.

Formula

  • Studs along the wall = round up (wall length ÷ spacing) + 1. This puts a stud at both ends of the wall even when the length is not a multiple of the spacing, and never gives fewer than 2.
  • Studs before waste = studs along the wall + openings × extra studs per opening + corners × extra studs per corner.
  • Studs to buy = studs before waste × (1 + waste %), rounded up.
  • Plate length = wall length × number of plates; plate boards = plate length ÷ board length, rounded up.

Example: a 12 ft wall, studs 16 in on center, one opening, no corners, 10 % waste: 144 ÷ 16 = 9, + 1 = 10 studs along the wall, + 2 for the opening = 12, × 1.10 = 13.2, so buy 14 studs. Three plates make 36 ft of plate, which is 3 boards of 12 ft.

Example: a 3.6 m wall, studs 400 mm on center, no openings, 10 % waste: 3600 ÷ 400 = 9, + 1 = 10 studs, × 1.10 = 11 studs. Three plates make 10.8 m of plate, which is 3 boards of 4.8 m.

Metric spacings of 300, 400 and 600 mm are close to, but not the same as, 12, 16 and 24 in (305, 406 and 610 mm).

What is not counted

  • Headers, cripple studs, sills, blocking and fire blocking.
  • Extra studs for point loads, shear walls or other engineered framing.
  • The wall height is used only to show the stud length: wall height minus the plates (1.5 in each38 mm each). Precut studs (92⅝ in92⅝ in (2353 mm)) are made for 8 ft walls with three plates and leave room for drywall.

The counting method and extra studs are estimating conventions, not a code. Your plans, local code and a licensed builder decide the actual framing.

FAQ

How many studs do I need for a wall?

Divide the wall length by the spacing, round up and add one for the end, then add studs for openings and corners and a waste allowance. A 12 ft wall at 16 in on center with one opening needs 14 studs with 10 % waste.A 3.6 m wall at 400 mm on center with no openings needs 11 studs with 10 % waste.

Why add one stud?

The spacing counts the gaps between studs. A wall with 9 gaps has 10 studs, because there is a stud at both ends.

How many extra studs does a door or window need?

A typical opening has a king stud and a jack stud on each side (4 studs), but some of them replace regular studs. The default of 2 extra studs per opening is an estimating assumption; change it to match your plan.

Does the calculator include headers and blocking?

No. Headers, cripples, sills and blocking depend on the opening sizes and your framing plan, so add them separately.

What waste allowance should I use?

10 % is a common allowance for crooked or split studs and cutting mistakes. Use less if you hand-pick your lumber.
